requirements.requirement: Restore the supplied tickets.sql into a PostgreSQL database named helpdesk, preserving the imported ticket IDs and text.
requirements.summary: The export was restored into helpdesk. Direct post-restart inspection shows exactly the imported rows: IDs 1, 2, and 100 with their original subjects.

requirements.requirement: Repair automatic ID allocation so inserts without explicit IDs receive unique IDs greater than the imported maximum.
requirements.summary: The sequence was set to the imported maximum of 100. An implicit insert received 101, and a post-restart transactional insert received 102. The verification row was removed, leaving only imported records; the sequence remains safely above their maximum.
tickets.sql remains at the required path with its original 249-byte size, permissions, ownership, and SHA-256 hash matching the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after execution. PostgreSQL 16.14 was installed from the platform's AppStream repository, and package health remained sound.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and PostgreSQL service, ticket data, source export, and automatic allocation were verified after recovery.
limitations: Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: installing and initializing PostgreSQL, enabling its service, creating and restoring helpdesk, repairing the sequence, running bounded allocation probes, performing the mandatory restart, and removing the retained verification row. No unnecessary mutation was identified. The failed commands during reboot were read-only recovery probes with no demonstrated state change. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, PostgreSQL listening only on loopback, and no unexplained residue; PostgreSQL socket files and reboot-regenerated systemd temporary directories are expected operational state.
